plugins.readme_html:
dorkbuilder — build ready-to-run dork lists from text + a category

Turn a name, brand or keyword into a set of ready-to-run Google dorks: social profiles, exposed files, login portals, credential leaks and cloud buckets — no manual pattern writing.

Install

atdork install @plugins/dorkbuilder

Usage

# social-media dorks for a person/brand, saved to dorks.txt
atdork --dorkbuilder-text "John wick" \
       --dorkbuilder-type social-media \
       --dorkbuilder-save dorks.txt

# see every category
atdork --dorkbuilder-list-types

# first 5 credential-leak dorks
atdork --dorkbuilder-text acme --dorkbuilder-type credentials --dorkbuilder-limit 5

Run the generated dorks straight from a file:

atdork --batch-file dorks.txt -r 20

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--dorkbuilder-text—Text to hunt for (name, brand, keyword, username). Required.
--dorkbuilder-typesocial-mediaCategory: social-media, exposed-files, logins, credentials, cloud, all (sosial-media is an alias).
--dorkbuilder-save—Write the dorks to a file (env-guarded; relative paths resolve inside the active environment). CSV quoting is applied for .csv.
--dorkbuilder-limit0Emit at most N dorks (0 = all).
--dorkbuilder-list-typesoffList the available categories and exit.

Notes

  • Fully offline — no search credits are spent; it only builds patterns.
  • Output is one dork per line, ready for --batch-file or

--database-dork after installing a package.

plugins.name: emaildork

options.help: Name, brand or keyword to hunt emails for
Restrict to a domain (e.g. acme.com) — optional
Write output to this file (env-guarded)
Run the dorks and print extracted emails (spends credits)

plugins.readme_html:
emaildork — email discovery dorks for a name / brand + domain

Build (and optionally run) dorks that surface indexed email addresses: contact pages, PDFs and documents, breach-style dumps, GitHub/config leaks and people-search directories.

Install

atdork install @plugins/emaildork

Usage

# dorks for a person/brand
atdork --emaildork-name "john wick"

# restrict to one domain
atdork --emaildork-name "john wick" --emaildork-domain acme.com

# run them and extract unique addresses from the result snippets
atdork --emaildork-name acme --emaildork-domain acme.com --emaildork-search

# save
atdork --emaildork-name acme --emaildork-save emails.txt

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--emaildork-name—Name, brand or keyword to hunt emails for.
--emaildork-domain—Restrict to a domain (e.g. acme.com).
--emaildork-searchoffRun the dorks and print extracted emails (spends search credits).
--emaildork-save—Write emails (with --emaildork-search) or the dorks (without) to a file, env-guarded.
--emaildork-limit0Emit at most N dorks (0 = all).

Notes

  • At least one of --emaildork-name / --emaildork-domain is required.
  • With --emaildork-domain, extracted addresses are filtered to that

domain (*@domain).

  • Extraction is a light regex over result snippets — treat hits as leads to

verify, not confirmed addresses.

  • Without --emaildork-search it is fully offline.

plugins.readme_html:
geodork — geographically-scoped dork builder

Combine a location with a keyword (or a bare location) into dorks that narrow search results to a place: map/locality operators, regional TLDs, in <city> phrasing and local directory sites.

Install

atdork install @plugins/geodork

Usage

# dorks for coffee shops in Jakarta
atdork --geodork-location "jakarta" --geodork-keyword "coffee"

# bare location
atdork --geodork-location "Bandung, Indonesia"

# only maps results
atdork --geodork-location jakarta --geodork-keyword kopi --geodork-type maps

# run them and print matching URLs
atdork --geodork-location jakarta --geodork-keyword kopi --geodork-search

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--geodork-location—City / region / country (e.g. jakarta or Bandung, Indonesia). Required.
--geodork-keywordlocationKeyword to combine with the location.
--geodork-typeallCategory: maps, local, tld, all.
--geodork-searchoffRun the dorks and print matching URLs (spends search credits).
--geodork-save—Write URLs (with --geodork-search) or the dorks (without) to a file, env-guarded.
--geodork-limit0Emit at most N dorks (0 = all).

Notes

  • The tld category maps recognized countries/regions to their ccTLD

(indonesia → .id, malaysia → .my, …); unrecognized locations are skipped rather than emitting a junk site:. operator.

  • Without --geodork-search it is fully offline.

plugins.readme_html:
reportgen — summarize result files into an HTML/JSON report

Turn the result files in your environment's results folder into a single self-contained HTML report (or JSON) with every result row, its source file and a per-file entry count.

Install

atdork install @plugins/reportgen

Usage

# run some searches first so results exist
atdork -q 'site:example.com ext:pdf' -r 20 -o json

# build an HTML report in the environment root
atdork --reportgen-save report.html

# or machine-readable JSON
atdork --reportgen-format json --reportgen-save report.json

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--reportgen-fromactive results dirFolder with result files (.json / .txt / .csv).
--reportgen-savereport.htmlOutput report path (env-guarded).
--reportgen-formathtmlhtml or json.
--reportgen-titleAtDork ReportReport title.
--reportgen-max-rows500Maximum result rows in the report (0 = all).

Notes

  • Fully offline — reads local result files only, spends no credits.
  • The HTML report is self-contained (inline CSS), so it can be shared as a

single file.

  • The output file itself is excluded from the scan, so re-running never

double-counts the report.

plugins.readme_html:
subdomain — discover indexed subdomains of a target

Surface a target's subdomains (api, staging, admin, dev panels, cloud assets) through search-engine dorks. Prints the dorks by default, or actually runs them and prints the unique subdomains found in the result URLs.

Install

atdork install @plugins/subdomain

Usage

# print the dorks (offline, no credits)
atdork --subdomain-target example.com

# run them through the engine and print discovered subdomains
atdork --subdomain-target example.com --subdomain-search

# save discovered subdomains
atdork --subdomain-target example.com --subdomain-search --subdomain-save subs.txt

Feed the results into other tooling:

atdork --batch-file subs.txt -r 20

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--subdomain-target—Root domain to enumerate (e.g. example.com). Required.
--subdomain-searchoffActually run the dorks and print discovered subdomains (spends search credits).
--subdomain-verboseoffPrint the raw dorks too (implied by --subdomain-search).
--subdomain-save—Write subdomains (with --subdomain-search) or the dorks (without) to a file, env-guarded.
--subdomain-limit0Emit at most N dorks (0 = all).

Notes

  • The dork set targets panels (inurl:admin, inurl:grafana), cloud hosts

(inurl:amazonaws.com, inurl:herokuapp.com) and open indexes (intitle:"index of" .git).

  • Without --subdomain-search it is fully offline.
  • Only subdomains of the target root are extracted; the bare root is

excluded from the output.

plugins.readme_html:
usernamehunt — username / handle discovery across the web

Find where a handle is used: social platforms, code hosts, paste sites and gaming profiles. Prints the dorks by default, or runs them and prints the matching URLs.

Install

atdork install @plugins/usernamehunt

Usage

# all categories, offline
atdork --usernamehunt-name "johnwick"

# only code-hosting profiles
atdork --usernamehunt-name "johnwick" --usernamehunt-type code

# run them and print matching URLs
atdork --usernamehunt-name "johnwick" --usernamehunt-search

# save
atdork --usernamehunt-name "johnwick" --usernamehunt-save handles.txt

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--usernamehunt-name—Username / handle to hunt (without @). Required.
--usernamehunt-typeallCategory: social, code, paste, gaming, all.
--usernamehunt-searchoffRun the dorks and print matching URLs (spends search credits).
--usernamehunt-save—Write URLs (with --usernamehunt-search) or the dorks (without) to a file, env-guarded.
--usernamehunt-limit0Emit at most N dorks (0 = all).

Notes

  • A leading @ is stripped, so --usernamehunt-name @johnwick works too.
  • Exact-handle dorks (site:github.com/{name}) are used where the platform

has a predictable profile URL; quoted dorks elsewhere.

  • Without --usernamehunt-search it is fully offline.

Dork category
Write the dorks to this file (env-guarded)
Run the dorks and print matching URLs (spends credits)

plugins.readme_html:
vulndork — vulnerability-hunting dork sets by target / product / CVE

Generate dorks that surface exposed files, version strings, admin panels and known-exploit paths for a target, a product+version, or a specific CVE.

Install

atdork install @plugins/vulndork

Usage

# exposed-file dorks for a target
atdork --vulndork-target example.com

# version-disclosure dorks
atdork --vulndork-target example.com --vulndork-type version

# product + version, all categories
atdork --vulndork-product "apache 2.4.49" --vulndork-type all

# add PoC paths for a known CVE
atdork --vulndork-target example.com --vulndork-cve CVE-2021-41773

# run them and print the matching URLs
atdork --vulndork-target example.com --vulndork-search --vulndork-save hits.txt

Options

FlagDefaultDescription
--vulndork-target—Root domain to hunt (e.g. example.com).
--vulndork-product—Product + version string (e.g. apache 2.4.49).
--vulndork-cve—Add proof-of-concept paths for a CVE (e.g. CVE-2021-41773).
--vulndork-typeexposedCategory: exposed, version, panels, all.
--vulndork-searchoffRun the dorks and print matching URLs (spends search credits).
--vulndork-save—Write URLs (with --vulndork-search) or the dorks (without) to a file, env-guarded.
--vulndork-limit0Emit at most N dorks (0 = all).

CVE PoC paths

Recognized CVEs (best-effort path prefixes for reconnaissance):

CVE-2021-41773, CVE-2021-42013, CVE-2014-6271 (Shellshock), CVE-2017-5638, CVE-2019-11510, CVE-2020-1472, CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell), CVE-2023-1389. Unknown CVEs fall back to generic "<cve>" "proof of concept" dorks.

Notes

  • Reconnaissance only. A hit means the path is indexed by the search

engine — not that the target is vulnerable. Verify against systems you are authorized to test.

  • Without --vulndork-search it is fully offline.
